title: Our Country—India
parentNotes: Geography Ch 7, pages 52–56, the whole chapter, from the same scan as History Ch 4 and Civics Ch 4. Approved straight away at your request.
No answer key is printed. Answers come from the chapter text.
Book misprint: p.54 gives the westernmost point as 68° 7′ W, but p.53 and Ex. III Q2 use 68° 7′ E. The app uses E.
Ex. IV Q3 (needsReview): the pages never say why peninsular India stays warm; the model answer uses only where the Tropic of Cancer is (p.53). Please check with her teacher.
Ex. IV Q6 (needsReview): an opinion question ("good or bad?"). The model answer uses p.52; her reasons may differ.
Ex. I Q5 asks for the capital of her own state or UT; it is a think-and-write here, because the answer depends on where you live.
Ex. II asks her to correct the false sentences; the app shows the correction after she answers.
The book has no section V in the exercises (IV is followed by VI). Ex. VI map work is in the notebook tasks of lessons 2 and 3.
Lead In, Do and learn and Enrichment activities are class work and are not questions here.

lessons.title: India: size, people and location

videos.title: India location and extent class 6 (parent to choose)

cards.title: A land of variety
cards.body: India, that is Bharat, is a vast land with immense geographical and cultural variations: towering mountains, extensive plains and plateaus, rivers, deserts and long coastlines. Its flora and fauna are rich and varied, and each region has its own languages, traditional clothes and distinct foods.
cards.reveal: Despite the great diversities of this land, there is an underlying unity that binds this nation together.

cards.title: Big and busy
cards.body: India is spread over an area of 3.28 million sq. km, making it the seventh largest country in the world. It has overtaken China to become the most populous country, with 1.426 billion people (as of 2023). It is the largest democracy in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: India has almost 18% of the world’s population, but only 2.4% of the total land area.

cards.title: A peninsula
cards.body: India is located in the southern part of the continent of Asia. It is a peninsula. "A peninsula is a land surrounded by water on three sides."
cards.example: The Himalayas in the north, the Indian Ocean in the south, the Arabian Sea in the west and the Bay of Bengal in the east.

cards.title: Hemispheres
cards.body: India is located in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres. The Tropic of Cancer passes through almost the centre of India.

cards.title: Latitude and longitude
cards.body: The Indian mainland extends from 8° 4′ N to 37° 6′ N latitude (south to north), and 68° 7′ E to 97° 25′ E longitude (west to east).

lessons.title: India’s extent, time and neighbours

videos.title: Indian Standard Time and India’s neighbours (parent to choose)

cards.title: North to south
cards.body: The northernmost point of India lies in the Siachen Glacier region of the Karakoram range (37° 6′ N). The southernmost point of the Indian mainland lies at Kanniyakumari (Kanyakumari) (8° 4′ N). The distance between these two points is 3,214 km.

cards.title: East to west
cards.body: The easternmost point of India lies in Arunachal Pradesh (97° 25′ E). The westernmost point lies in the Rann of Kutchch in Gujarat (68° 7′ E). The distance between these two points is 2,933 km.

cards.title: Indian Standard Time
cards.body: The longitudinal width of India is almost 30°. The time lag between the easternmost and the westernmost parts of India is two hours. To avoid confusion, India follows the time at the central or standard meridian of India (82° 30′ E). This is called the Indian Standard Time (IST).

cards.title: Coastline and border
cards.body: The length of India’s coastline (its maritime boundary) is 7,516 km. The length of India’s terrestrial border is 15,200 km.

cards.title: Neighbours by land
cards.body: Seven countries share terrestrial (land) boundaries with India. Pakistan and Afghanistan lie to the north-west, Bangladesh and Myanmar to the east, and China, Nepal and Bhutan to the north.

cards.title: Neighbours across the sea
cards.body: Across the sea, to the south, India’s neighbours are the islands of Sri Lanka and the Maldives. India is separated from Sri Lanka by the Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar.

lessons.title: States and union territories

videos.title: States and union territories of India (parent to choose)

cards.title: Free India, made of states
cards.body: After more than 200 years under British rule, India became independent on 15 August 1947. For better administration, India was divided into states on the basis of language.

cards.title: 28 states and 8 union territories
cards.body: Today India has 28 states and 8 union territories. India’s capital is New Delhi. Rajasthan is the largest state and Goa is the smallest state.

cards.title: State or union territory?
cards.body: A state is a smaller territorial division of India, each having its own duly elected state government. A union territory is a part of the country that is under the direct administration of the Union Government.

cards.title: Some state capitals
cards.body: Andhra Pradesh: Amaravati · Assam: Dispur · Karnataka: Bengaluru · Kerala: Thiruvananthapuram · Maharashtra: Mumbai · Tamil Nadu: Chennai · Telangana: Hyderabad · West Bengal: Kolkata. All 28 are in the table on p.54.
cards.reveal: Chandigarh is the capital of both Punjab and Haryana, and is itself a union territory.

cards.title: The 8 union territories
cards.body: Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Sri Vijaya Puram, Port Blair) · Chandigarh · Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Daman) · Lakshadweep (Kavaratti) · Puducherry · National Capital Territory, Delhi (New Delhi) · Jammu & Kashmir (Srinagar in summer / Jammu in winter) · Ladakh (Leh).

questionBank.prompt: India has ____ % of the world’s population.
questionBank.explanation: India accounts for almost 18% of the world’s population (p.52).

questionBank.prompt: India is the second largest country in the world.
questionBank.explanation: India is the seventh largest country in the world (p.52).

questionBank.prompt: The Tropic of Capricorn runs through the middle of India.
questionBank.explanation: It is the Tropic of Cancer that passes through almost the centre of India (p.53).

questionBank.prompt: India is located in the Northern Hemisphere.
questionBank.explanation: India is located in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres (p.53).

questionBank.prompt: The Indian mainland extends from:
options: 37° 6′ N to 8° 4′ N latitude; and 68° 7′ E to 97° 25′ E longitude
37° 6′ E to 8° 4′ E latitude; and 68° 7′ N to 97° 25′ N longitude
30° 5′ N to 8° 4′ S latitude; and 68° 7′ E to 97° 25′ W longitude
37° 6′ S to 8° 4′ N longitude; and 68° 7′ E to 97° 25′ W latitude
questionBank.answer: 37° 6′ N to 8° 4′ N latitude; and 68° 7′ E to 97° 25′ E longitude
questionBank.explanation: Latitude is N, longitude is E: 8° 4′ N to 37° 6′ N and 68° 7′ E to 97° 25′ E (p.53).

questionBank.prompt: How is India a peninsula?
questionBank.modelAnswer: A peninsula is a land surrounded by water on three sides. India is bounded by the Arabian Sea in the west, the Bay of Bengal in the east and the Indian Ocean in the south, with the Himalayas in the north.
questionBank.explanation: p.53 has the definition and the four boundaries.

questionBank.prompt: Why does most of peninsular India remain warm throughout the year?
questionBank.modelAnswer: The Tropic of Cancer passes through almost the centre of India, so most of peninsular India lies to the south of it. It is also surrounded by the sea on three sides.
questionBank.explanation: p.53 only says where the Tropic of Cancer is; ask your teacher for the full reason.

questionBank.prompt: India is a land of great diversity. Do you think it is good or bad for the country? Give reasons to support your answer.
questionBank.modelAnswer: For example: good. The mountains, plains, plateaus, rivers, deserts and coastlines, the rich and varied flora and fauna, and the many languages, clothes and foods make the country rich and varied. And despite the great diversities, there is an underlying unity that binds the nation together.
questionBank.explanation: There is no single answer. Use the facts on p.52 for your reasons.

questionBank.prompt: The southernmost point of the Indian mainland lies at ____.
questionBank.explanation: The southernmost point of the Indian mainland lies at Kanniyakumari (Kanyakumari) (p.54).

questionBank.prompt: The Palk Strait lies between India and the Maldives.
questionBank.explanation: India is separated from Sri Lanka by the Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar (p.54).

questionBank.prompt: Which of the following countries is not a neighbour of India?
questionBank.explanation: Pakistan, Bhutan and China are in the list of neighbours on p.54; Japan is not.

questionBank.prompt: Which of the following states will be the first to experience sunrise?
questionBank.explanation: The easternmost point of India lies in Arunachal Pradesh (p.54), so the Sun rises there first.

questionBank.prompt: Which of the following countries can India have overseas trade with?
questionBank.explanation: Overseas means across the sea. The Maldives is a neighbour across the sea; the others share land borders (p.54).

questionBank.prompt: The Sun rises in Arunachal Pradesh two hours before it rises in Gujarat. Explain why this is so.
questionBank.modelAnswer: Arunachal Pradesh has the easternmost point of India (97° 25′ E) and Gujarat the westernmost (68° 7′ E). The longitudinal width of India is almost 30°, so the time lag between the easternmost and westernmost parts is two hours. The Sun rises first in the east.
questionBank.explanation: p.54: the extent east to west, and the two-hour time lag.

questionBank.prompt: Name India’s neighbours.
questionBank.modelAnswer: By land: Pakistan and Afghanistan (north-west), China, Nepal and Bhutan (north), and Bangladesh and Myanmar (east). Across the sea, to the south: Sri Lanka and the Maldives.
questionBank.explanation: All nine are on p.54.

questionBank.prompt: The capital of India is ____.
questionBank.explanation: India’s capital is New Delhi (p.54).

questionBank.prompt: The largest state in India is ____.
questionBank.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest state (p.54).

questionBank.prompt: The capital of the state or union territory to which you belong is ____.
questionBank.modelAnswer: Find your state or union territory in the table on p.54 and write its capital. Ask a grown-up if you are not sure.
questionBank.explanation: Your answer depends on where you live. Check it in the table on p.54.

questionBank.prompt: There are 28 states and 9 union territories in India.
questionBank.explanation: There are 28 states and 8 union territories (p.54).

questionBank.prompt: What is the difference between a state and a union territory in India? Give two examples of each.
questionBank.modelAnswer: A state is a smaller territorial division of India with its own duly elected state government, for example Kerala and Rajasthan. A union territory is a part of the country under the direct administration of the Union Government, for example Lakshadweep and Puducherry.
questionBank.explanation: Definitions: p.55. Examples: any from the table on p.54.

questionBank.explanation: p.54 union territory table.

questionBank.prompt: Chandigarh is the capital of
questionBank.explanation: The capital of Chandigarh, Haryana and Punjab are at Chandigarh (p.53 map note, p.54 table).

questionBank.prompt: For better administration, India was divided into states on the basis of ____.
